contents.text: ~2,000 years ago
Sage of the Stolen Flame taught people to use phlogiston and, together with Chaac, founded the Upper Sanctum, Hanan Pacha.
Chaac founded the first tribe.
Umoja Uenuku, one of the original six heroes of Natlan, met an Oceanid from Fontaine.
Uenuku joined the Grand Alliance.
Uenuku came under fire, but the Oceanid protected him at the cost of her life.
Uenuku left the Grand Alliance.
Natlan's best guide returned from the legendary mysterious island and founded the People of the Springs.
Atawallpa and his brother Waskar joined the scarlet-eyed youth to overthrow Och-Kan.
~500 years ago
Umoja Tupac, one of the six heroes of Natlan, was born in the People of the Springs.
The Cataclysm began.
Tupac joined Tenoch and five other heroes of Natlan to battle the Abyss.
Tupac was wounded in the battle, but managed to carry the Pyro Archon Mavuika to the Sacred Flame before dying.
Cochanina became the Pyro Archon, banishing the Abyss from the lands of the People of the Springs.
Ten years after the Cataclysm, the legend of the Jade of Return emerged.
A group of various tribes, including a Mountain Ranger from the People of the Springs, set out for Ochkanatlan in search of the Jade of Return.
The Jade of Return turned out to be a trap, and almost the entire group was killed.
Present Day
The Night Kingdom was nearly dissolved in the Abyss, and its attacks became more frequent.
Elder Atea was wounded by a monster, and the Abyssal energy began to corrode her body.
Amina became the tribe's chief.
Umoja Mualani set out to rescue her friend from the Night Kingdom and was recognized by her Ancient Name, becoming one of the six heroes of Natlan.
The Abyss launched a full-scale invasion of Natlan.
Atea perished.
The Pyro Archon used the power of the six heroes of Natlan, the Ruler of Death, and the divine throne to banish the Abyss.
The Abyss was destroyed.

<color=#ffd780>August 18, 2024</color>
Hello, Traveler!
Do you enjoy soaking in hot springs? If so, don't miss out on the "People of the Springs"! They have the best vacation spot, so let's learn more about them!
People of the Springs

The
are a tribe living on the Natlan seashore alongside the Koholasaurs. The tribe was founded on a small island, but later, water currents reshaped the landscape. Meztli was home to many legendary heroes: the first bearer of the Ancient Name
Uenuku, the heir to his Ancient Name, the giant Tupac, and Rangi Nui, to whom legends and songs were dedicated even after his death. According to the tribe's legends, Rangi Nui was both a sage who spoke to the heavens and a hero of the land, who stood upright between heaven and earth. When his soul returned to the rising sun, whereupon the sky itself became Rangi Nui.

This friendly tribe is passionate about music, parties, and hot springs. They live a carefree life, but some other tribes consider them lazy. The tribe's chief is Amina, but despite her young age, she is a responsible leader. Amina is highly intelligent and always full of brilliant ideas. She developed a battle preparation and defense facilities renovation plan, as well as her personnel deployment plan. The Meztli hot springs are rich in phlogiston and are believed to have the power to cure illnesses. Visitors come not only from all over Natlan but also from all over Teyvat. However, despite their popularity, using the hot springs can be dangerous for unprepared tourists, as the high temperatures can cause burns or loss of consciousness. Slipping and falling on rocks is also common. Due to the location of the People of the Springs, the tribe is famous for its water sports: surfing, beach volleyball, diving, water polo, and parasailing. Moreover, the tribe members are Natlan's best guides and love to explore. Their work is similar to that of adventurers, but the People of the Springs' guides can explore lands where temperatures are high or areas covered in liquid phlogiston with the help of Koholasaurs. Therefore, both members of other tribes and foreign tourists often hire the Meztli guides to show them the shortest route or blaze a new trail.

According to legend, the first chief and founder of the People of the Springs was the best guide in all of Natlan. At first, he was like a treasure hunter. He pursued results, overcoming countless dangers to prove his worth. Again and again, he strove to reach places others feared to tread, bringing back rare treasures. The first chief was at the height of his glory, but he still couldn't get enough. Then he found a new goal — a challenge no one had ever mastered — the legendary, mysterious island. The first chief's friends, who had traveled with him all this time, grew weary of the danger and warned him against the journey, but they nevertheless agreed to go with him. As before, they devised various ways to move forward and never failed the chief, even when he entrusted them with his life. They always trusted him, even when it required great courage. Finally, they reached their goal. The mysterious island shone with a golden light; countless treasures were buried there, and the golden glow was baiting him towards death. But the glow of rare ores was also a warning sign of an impending eruption. He could risk his life and claim the treasure, but he risked losing his friends. Ultimately, he decided to return without a treasure. Everyone was disappointed that the renowned guide returned empty-handed, but when he saw that everyone had returned alive, he was satisfied for the first time. Perhaps the treasure he was truly searching for had been nearby all along. So the guide decided to end his long journey and find a safe place for his hard-earned treasure, becoming the first chief of the People of the Springs. For him, this was the real mysterious island.

The first chief left clues to the mysterious island so that everyone could travel there. Only a few could overcome this arduous journey, entrusting their lives to their friends, and discover the legendary treasure. But those who did, each time, made the same decision as the first chief. There's a saying among the guides of the People of the Springs, <color=#ffffffd9>"If the goal of the journey was to reach the destination, then you should have never left the house to begin with."</color>

Over time, some unscrupulous guides began charging tourists and tribe members Mora, promising to lead them to the mysterious island. They forced them to buy expensive equipment at special stores and spend Mora on photographs with a Koholasaurus, which, they claimed, could reveal the secret of safe passage. Others simply boasted that they had already visited the legendary island many times. A man considered the tribe's best guide once claimed to have reached the mysterious island alone. And since no one else had been there, no one could disprove his claim. It later turned out that he had made it all up for the sake of his reputation, and those who had actually visited the island kept their journey a secret.

One of the guides who actually visited the mysterious island is the tribe's hero, Mualani. The girl decided to become a guide after traveling through Natlan, when people began asking her to show them the way to dragon ruins, where no one had ever been. She thought it all sounded very doable, so the next day, she went and found the famous guide, Nuu, and asked to be his student. She asked him what skills a guide who wants to take people exploring needs to master. Nuu thought for a second: <color=#ffffffd9>"First is wilderness survival, such as the behaviors of wild animals, the uses of and how to cook common plants, and how to pick a good campsite. Next is knowing the land itself, such as how to judge the direction of the tides and the length of time between eruptions. You must also have actually traveled across the landscape, traversing the canyons, caves, and volcanoes. Yes, spend about three years doing that, and you'll be ready to start learning."</color> The girl was about to turn and leave, but suddenly thought better of it. Although her mentor emphasized that the most important thing was to reach their destination safely, Mualani could never resist looking at where the other fork in the road led. When she officially became a guide, she began planning the safest and most reliable routes for travelers, but a journey without happy accidents would be like an Apple Roly Poly without Apple. One day, she led tourists to a plateau with a sweeping view and offered to take a photo when a volcano erupted in the distance. The tourists were frightened by the roar, but Mualani reassured them that at that distance, it was perfectly safe, so they could enjoy the show. Mualani is now a leading guide of the new generation, with extensive experience.
<color=#ffffffd9>"The most important thing on a journey is to have a good time on the way! The second most important is to pick a lucky time to set off!"</color>

customize.text: Uenuku, the Treader of the Rainbow

The first bearer of the Ancient Name
was Uenuku of the Meztli tribe. According to legend, several millennia ago, when dragons still ruled the future Natlan, the Oceanid Ianeira of Fontaine arrived at the springs at the behest of the Mistress of Many Waters, Egeria. She wanted to transform the searing waters of Natlan into clear springs and purge the water veins from flowing phlogiston, for the all-embracing love spread through the land along the flowing waters. The Oceanid explained that her ideal was the justice Uenuku sought. She offered to bless his spear with song and accompany him on his lonely journey in exchange for a spring where vicious beasts prowl. Although Uenuku had discerned the water fairy's true intentions and understood that she saw him as merely a means to fulfill an end, they still shared a common enemy, so he resolved to fight alongside her until the time came that they were to betray one another. Even if the Oceanid's words were simply designed to entice and everything dissipated into mist and rain, Uenuku would still have the justice he firmly believed in to "unite" the weak.

Ianeira was supposed to abandon the one with blind faith in justice. All she had to do was simply find another who could become King. She never cared for Uenuku's ideals, but just as spring waters have never taken a fixed form, so too do the hearts of humans and fairies sway with the night breeze. Uenuku joined the excavation of hollows in Ochkanatlan, and the Oceanid helped pump the water out. One day, Uenuku made a mistake and was on the verge of being consumed by the dragonlord's flames, but the Oceanid shielded him from the flames. As she died, she wondered if this might be the "communication and understanding" that the Mistress of Many Waters sought. She gave him one last smile, covering the sunlike blaze, leaving only rainbow hues in the rising vapor. After that, Uenuku left the Grand Alliance.

The scrolls passed down in the Meztli since time immemorial tell a completely different version of the legend. In this tale, the hero Uenuku met the Oceanid Ianeira, who came from foreign lands, and fell in love with her. In a moment of suspicion, he was separated from his beloved, but then, filled with regret, Uenuku wandered every inch of the scorched lands, searching only for his beloved. After decades of relentless pursuit, the water sprite's hardened heart softened, finally showing a trace of compassion. She plucked a soft cloud from the sky and turned it into a rainbow, guiding the hero towards the other side of the sea. Blessed by the Sacred Flame, Uenuku and his lover were finally reunited, never to be separated again. The tribal elders believe that the shells we see today are fragments of the rainbow that fell into the sea back then. Each shell is always formed with two connected sides, symbolizing a wish for reunion.

customize.text: The Fall of Ochkanatlan

When Xbalanque arose from the throne to enter the Sacred Flame, the mortal world awaited the arrival of their successor. His best friend, Och-Kan, decided that the Pyro Archon should forever remain the one and only. He became the ruler of the first city, which was named Ochkanatlan, and led the Grand Alliance to unite all the tribes under its rule. He wanted to create an ideal world for humans, one in which there was no place for the descendants of the ancient dragons, so he issued an order to exterminate them. To harness dragon technology, he opened the door to malevolent forces, leading Ochkanatlan to the Abyssal corrosion. At first, the Abyssal corrosion remained within the controllable range, and Och-Kan hoped that people would gradually adapt to it. But suddenly, during repairs, overnight, a deep well was completely submerged by a dark calamity, and all nearby residents were transformed into monsters. Although Och-Kan strove to continue Xbalanque's legacy, he became a tyrant to the people he considered his own. To them, Och-Kan was no different from the evil dragons that ruled Natlan, and the people called upon a new Pyro Archon to overthrow the tyrant.

A rebellion against the tyrant Och-Kan was led by a scarlet-eyed youth from the Flower-Feather Clan. He was joined by the twin brothers, Atawallpa and Waskar, noble sons of Meztli and Teteocan, who loved to joke around. The elder Atawallpa had lips and teeth that were sharper than any blade and was an incorrigible chatterbox, while the younger Waskar’s back still bore the brunt of the tyrant's lash. With them were Sakkuk, the daughter of the mines, Yupanqui, an old friend of Xbalanque and Och-Kan, and the artisan Manqu. He recounted the incredible trials he had endured in Ochkanatlan, but the twins took the story as but a tale. When the scarlet-eyed youth led them to Ochkanatlan, those who came from the spring's source believed it was a time for those who had forgotten their past to listen anew to the echoes of the waves. And on that day, the eloquent Atawallpa rekindled the desire of all for past glories. And although the tyrant of Ochkanatlan was overthrown, Yupanqui and Manqu couldn’t leave the city, and Atawallpa’s tormented wails wracked his throat hoarse upon witnessing his brother die at the hands of their adversary.

customize.text: The Cataclysm

Five hundred years ago, the Cataclysm began across Teyvat, a black wave of Abyss engulfed all seven kingdoms, and Natlan was no exception. The waters of the People of the Springs were polluted, and the land of the Children of Echoes was covered with dangerous mud. Black winds ravaged the lands of the Flower-Feather Clan, and the already specific and fragile Ley Lines of Natlan were completely devastated. At first, the Natlanese believed that destruction was the Abyss's primary instinct, but its methods began to confirm its intelligence. Each disaster seemed to be specially "designed" for each tribe. The first to rise against the disaster was Tenoch, exiled from his tribe and stripped of his Ancient Name. He was joined by five heroes bearing the Ancient Names of the first Pyro Archon's companions.

Last to join Tenoch was the greatest enemy from his youth, the giant Tupac of the People of the Springs. He stood out from the crowd due to his enormous height, and there was no one in Natlan taller or stronger than him. The mighty giant bore the Ancient Name
Fifteen hundred years earlier, this same name had been borne by Uenuku, who traveled with the first Pyro Archon, Xbalanque. The mountain-like Tupac had always been a true hero. Once, in a fit of rage, he shattered mountains with his bare hands and thrust rocks into the earth to make hot springs bubble up. He ventured alone into the sea, battled a two-tailed whale, and tore out the fierce beast's teeth to carry with him. During the battles between Tupac and Tenoch, the giant was left with over three hundred scars, twenty broken bones, and over one hundred obsidian shards lodged deep within his body. The giant himself left the hero with two hundred minor wounds, two broken ribs, and an eye that could no longer perceive distance. They recalled all their scars, then burst into riotous laughter, joined hands, and thus, Tenoch found allies from the six tribes, becoming the leader of the united army of Natlan. During the final battle, which the heroes embarked on with the Pyro Archon, the mountain-like Tupac was the last surviving hero and carried the Archon to the Sacred Flame before his death so that she could give up her life and be reborn many years later.

Ten years after the Cataclysm, when the Abyss had retreated, a legend emerged in Natlan of the Jade of Return, an ancient treasure kept in the forbidden city of Ochkanatlan, capable of destroying the Abyss forever. People, desperate to fight the Abyss, decided to try their luck and search for the Jade, even if it meant a trap. Among these people was a team led by a warrior from the Flower-Feather Clan, which included a Mountain Ranger from the People of the Springs, who was supposed to reclaim his home. When they arrived in Ochkanatlan, it turned out that the Jade of Return was a myth, created by the
In reality, the Jade of Return was half a core needed to activate an ancient dragon weapon capable of destroying the Abyss at the cost of all life in Natlan. The Jade of Return was sealed so that only humans could remove it, so Waxaklahun Ubah Kan himself could not obtain it. Thus, he created a legend to attract humans. At the legendary Tonatiuh and in the forbidden city, the entire group perished in the battle with Och-Kan, who was corrupted by the Abyss.

customize.text: The War with the Abyss

Although the Abyss was defeated during the Cataclysm, it did not vanish completely, but rather retreated into the depths of the Night Kingdom. Gradually, over the course of five hundred years, the Abyss began to attack Natlan. The Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame and the Night Warden Wars were initiated to bolster the protection of the Sacred Flame. During the Pilgrimage, participants first competed against each other under the guidance of bearers of an Ancient Name, and then members of the winning teams earned the right to fight one-on-one duels. The Pilgrimage selected the strongest warriors from each tribe to fight the Abyss in defense of their homeland. Their names and deeds were captured in epic tales, and thanks to the Archon's blessing, called the Ode of Resurrection, the victors could be resurrected even if they died.
Although the war between Natlan and the Abyss has lasted for centuries, and the Natlanese grew up on stories and legendary heroes who fought the Abyss, life among the People of the Springs has always remained calm and measured. When elders decided to discuss an important matter, they'd usually take a nice, comfy soak in the hot springs first, then enjoy some snacks along with milk before finally slowly getting around to the actual business. When children asked if the Abyss was so dangerous and why no one was worried, the adults replied that they, too, could defeat it when they grew up. But while the People of the Springs' life was still filled with parties at the hot springs, attacks from the Abyss became more frequent and dangerous. Several years ago, the Abyss attacked the tribe in the middle of the night. The tribe's hero, Mualani, who had no combat experience at the time, like her friends, wanted to stay and help the warriors. They set out to warn nearby residents, patrol the area, provide first aid, and mark the enemy's locations. Mualani, the fastest of them, set out to survey the area around the tribe along the spiritual paths, marking the locations of Abyssal Pylons. Each time she found one, she relayed the information to the battling guardians. They encountered Pylons that spewed forth hordes of monsters, and the warriors engaged in a fierce battle with them. By the time Mualani managed to find reinforcements, the battlefield was already scorched and blackened. The renowned and experienced tribe elder, Atea, was fearlessly fighting the monsters when one of them appeared behind her, preparing to strike. Seeing Atea, Mualani rushed toward her and, in a leap, knocked the monster down, but in doing so, she herself was completely exposed. Challenged, the monster turned and raised its keen claws towards Mualani, but the attack never came. Atea's sharp steel pierced the monster's heart, and Mualani escaped with only a few scratches. Since that battle, she has been determined to become even faster and stronger, to be more useful.

During one battle, Atea was wounded in the stomach by a monster from the Abyss. Doctors managed to save her life, but the power of the Abyss remained in her body, and they made it clear that she could never bathe in the hot springs again. Immersion in hot water would accelerate the corrosion of her internal organs, and the disease would progress. For a long time, she lived, regretting that her illness prevented her from being on the front lines when her tribe faced ever greater challenges, but then she realized her body couldn't withstand it much longer. She began going to the hot springs again, unseen, and fighting monsters alone. When Atea's friends noticed her visiting the springs, they assumed she was feeling better and threw a party in her honor. But in reality, Atea had resigned herself to her imminent death, and even when the Traveler attempted to cleanse her body of the Abyss's power, it ingrained itself deep within her organs, leaving her as fragile as a dry leaf in the wind. When Atea realized her life force was waning, she gave the talisman to her hot springs friend, the Pyro Archon, Mavuika, as it <color=#ffffffd9>"embodies fond memories and my strength of will."</color> Shortly after the Abyss launched a full-scale invasion of Natlan, Atea the Candlekeeper perished, even in her final moments, thinking of protecting her tribe.

Five hundred years after the Cataclysm, the Abyss attacked Natlan again, and the People of the Springs were no exception. The Abyss's attack significantly weakened the tribe's defenses, and their lands were under attack. The Meztli's hero, Mualani, and chief Amina set out to help purify the waters near the tribe's settlement, while others headed north. On the border of Toyac Springs, Coatepec Mountain, and the Basin of Unnumbered Flames, the warriors and their Saurian companions found themselves trapped, and the attacks only grew stronger. The People of the Springs' warriors and their Saurians were making their way to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame when they were suddenly attacked by Abyssal monsters disguised as Saurians. The Saurians fought to the last, trying to protect the people, but even the arriving reinforcements were too late.

customize.text: Koholasaurs

In a time when the people of Natlan had not yet gathered into tribes and dragons ruled the land, there lived a young dragon who was unlike the others. In their pride, dragons have always looked down upon the other beings of this world, whether they were envoys of the heavens or puny mortal souls. But the young dragon Maawe, whose name meant "bit of string," loved to listen to the songs of the Monetoo and observe the lives of humans. It believed the beauty of a cool moonlit night and the warm shadows of red cliffs were more important than the true virtues of dragonkind. The dragon matriarch ordered Maawe to leave the tribe, for its heart had hardened, become as tenaciously proud as obsidian, and to be guided alone by cruel, lofty ambition.

It should have endured the scorching sun and barren wasteland to find ambition and fury, to cultivate a prideful, virtuous nature. Monetoo, that had accompanied it through all those innocent dreams, followed it, and the dragon was no longer alone. Together they journeyed east toward the high mountains shrouded in sulfurous clouds. There it reached the canyons, and there it stood before the pitch-black mines. Seeing its brethren seeking shiny crystals within the mountain, Maawe called out to greet them, but heard only its own echo in response. It turned out that the dragons living here had become accustomed to the stillness and silence and had been reduced to being creatures that lurked among the mountain rocks. Finding no fury there, Maawe shrugged and left.

Then it headed west toward the long-dead forest of mirk and gloom. It passed the remains of its ancestors, paying them respects as any dragon would, and approached a grand palace entwined with countless branches. Maawe called out to greet its kin flying freely through the canopy, but in response, it heard only the wind's rustling and swaying branches in return. It turned out that the dragons living here had become accustomed to the stillness and silence and had been reduced to being creatures that silently stalked the forest depths. Finding no fury there, Maawe shrugged and left. Maawe and the Monetoo traveled south to the brown prairies, where rivers had dried up. Maawe crossed a smoke-shrouded wasteland and saw his kinfallen into distant dreams among the fog. Maawe called out to greet them, and they responded warmly, inviting it to join them in wondrous dreaming. The glorious past and future of dragonkind shone forth, lit up by the miraculous luster of their fantasy. Maawe was about to succumb to this enchantment when it was suddenly awakened by the song of a friend. Unable to find fury here either, Maawe left this place. It then journeyed north to the untrodden edges of the land. It passed the lavaflow delta, crossed the silent, blistering wilderness, passed through lands where burning spirits danced, and entered cold obsidian gates. Finally, Maawe and the Monetoo stood before the high throne of a wise dragon, who asked what brought them here.

<color=#ffffffd9>"I thought that my brethren's hearts had all been hardened by the war with the heavens,</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>That the hatred that filled them had made them impervious to my advice.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>Yet today comes one before me, and such a young one at that.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>Tell me, what do you seek? Perhaps I might grant it as an exception."</color>

Maawe told the dragon of how the dragon tribe's matriarch had cast him out and sent him in search of fury, and of his own wanderings. The wise dragon replied that the fury the young dragon sought would not be found there and closed the obsidian gates before it. As Maawe returned, its faithful companion, deprived of light and warmth far from the phlogiston-rich land, turned as pale as ash, and its song grew distant and faint. Maawe desperately sought a way to save its companion, but the obsidian gates stayed firmly shut. Suddenly, the Monetoo asked Maawe to cast it into a sulfurous pool and bury it in the icy depths. Maawe wandered for a long time before reaching the sulfurous pools. Uninhabitable for living beings, it was a place where even getting close might result in being burned by toxic gases and scorched by boiling acid. But when Maawe scattered its companion's form into the sulfur, the boiling acid transformed into a clear spring. Thus, young Maawe created the first hot spring in Natlan and settled nearby. Its four limbs transformed into beautifully streamlined fins, its thin body became round, and thus it became the first of the Koholasaurs. Maawe never forgot its faithful companion and taught all the humans born from the springs the songs it had once heard and known. The first Meztli poets were born from the pure spring: <color=#ffffffd9>"Poets and bards are born of sulfur."</color> The poets who learned songs from Maawe became the ancestors of the People of the Springs' tribe.

customize.text: Akamai and Kau Kau

Among the People of the Springs, there once lived a famous explorer named Akamai. He and his friend, Koholasaurus Kau Kau, vowed to explore all of Natlan so that their deeds would be recorded on woven scrolls. For them, adventure and victory were a duty bestowed by the Wayob, and stories of mysterious islands and heroes of bygone days filled their hearts and minds. So, the young adventurers set out on their journey to perform a pilgrimage on foot. They intended to find a rich vein of ore or treasure, but treasures were far fewer in the world than intrepid explorers. The ore they dug up was mostly ordinary, as were the crystals they uncovered, but their joy never faded, and by the light of their nighttime bonfires, they held the stones they had collected. Akamai and Kau Kau recalled the events and feelings they experienced when they found them. They retrieved one stone from the claws of a giant Tepetlisaurus while traversing crystal-filled mountains. Another tripped them at the edge of a natural hot spring while they were drunk. A third stone, covered in ashes, once lay for a long time on the edge of an ancient city, burned to ash, until two travelers took it with them, paying no mind to the gray sentinel's wishes.
Together, Akamai and Kau Kau traveled throughout Natlan, filling their backpacks with countless beautiful stones and feasting on numerous delicious dishes. It is said that when they returned to the People of the Springs, Akamai had become much larger than he had been before. Years later, a descendant of Akamai wanted to emulate their forebear and set out on a journey. Akamai and Kau Kau decided to forge a blade for the scion to protect them from the dangers lurking in this world. And each time the smiths smelted the stones, the past was reawakened, coming to life with each memory spoken. When the great blade was forged, Akamai and Kau Kau presented it to the future wanderer as a parting gift.

<color=#ffffffd9>"Let the memories of the past accompany you on your journey, in place of forebears who now lack the strength to..."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"The past flows through the blood into each new generation, like an unquenchable fire passed down through rituals that never cease to burn."</color>
